name: Dardanelles
genZNote: The Dardanelles is the Bosporus's other half — together they're the two-strait combo that lets the Black Sea reach the rest of the world.

sections.heading: 🚨 Location & What It Connects
bullets: A natural strait in north-western Turkey, separating the European Gallipoli Peninsula from Asian mainland Turkey.
Connects the Sea of Marmara (and, beyond it via the Bosporus, the Black Sea) to the Aegean Sea and the wider Mediterranean.
Historically significant as the site of the Gallipoli campaign during World War I.

sections.heading: ⚓ Why It Matters
bullets: Forms the southern half of the two-strait route (Bosporus + Dardanelles) that is the Black Sea's only connection to open ocean shipping.
Also governed by the Montreux Convention (1936), the same treaty that regulates the Bosporus.
Important for grain and energy shipments leaving the Black Sea region bound for the Mediterranean and beyond.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Dardanelles is a strait in north-western Turkey linking the Sea of Marmara to the Aegean Sea, the southern half of the Black Sea's route to the Mediterranean.
keyFacts: In north-western Turkey, near the Gallipoli Peninsula.
Connects the Sea of Marmara to the Aegean Sea/Mediterranean.
Forms a pair with the Bosporus — together, the Black Sea's only sea route out.
Also governed by the Montreux Convention (1936).
commonConfusion: Bosporus = Black Sea end; Dardanelles = Mediterranean/Aegean end. Sea of Marmara sits between the two.

highYieldFacts: Dardanelles connects Sea of Marmara ↔ Aegean Sea/Mediterranean.
Forms the Black Sea's two-strait exit route together with the Bosporus.
Site of the WWI Gallipoli campaign.
commonTraps: Exam trap: naming only 'the Bosporus' as the Black Sea's route to the Mediterranean without also naming the Dardanelles — both straits are required.
mustRemember: Dardanelles = southern half of the Black Sea's two-strait exit; near Gallipoli.
